text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy. - - - -
-- Vietnam's Foreign Minister Nguyen Manh Cam called for an end to arbitrary embargoes and economic sanctions in a speech to the U.N. General Assembly earlier this week.
-- Vietnam has announced a new decree setting out procedural rules for visits by foreign warships.

-- Former Petrovietnam chief Ho Sy Thoang has said Vietnam will be pumping up to seven billion cubic metres of gas ashore each year by 1998 thanks to a new system of pipelines. Currently the level is around 300 million cubic metres. - - - -
-- The amended Vietnam Foreign Investment Law is expected to be endorsed at the coming National Assembly session scheduled to begin on October 15.
-- The head of state-owned Petrovietnam has said exploitation of at least three new oil fields and two gas fields will start in 1998. - - - -

-- Seven children have been killed, more than 43.600 houses submerged, 232 hectares (573 acres) of paddy field destroyed, and 3,026 households evacuated because of flash floods in the Mekong Delta provinces of southern Vietnam. - - - -

-- Vietnam's Asia Commercial joint-stock Bank (ACB) has received approval from the central State Bank to raise its registered capital from 70 billion VND ($6.36 million) to 300 billion VND ($27.27 million) and sell a 30 percent stake to foreign investors. - - - -
